artefact: outcome (policy) overlay — RULE-BASED notation (source of truth)
status: finalised (R2; Marc greenlit 2026-07-23; converged after 4 adversarial cross-examination rounds, ~90 agents). R3 (2026-07-28, S1): the lifecycle-distance term folded in and the relationship term moved onto the consensus stages. NO R2 rule value changed — the fold-in adds a multiplicative term and re-sources an existing one; both value sets are compiled from this file (see overlays/manifest.json). R5 (2026-08-19, Marc's failure-only ruling): the SUCCESS table is retired from the go-forward configuration — v4_failure_only compiles it as the constant 1.0 (rule 'passthrough', the multiplicative identity) so a success verdict routes on the base flow proportions unchanged, and only the failure table conditions. The five success rules below are RETAINED, unconsulted, so v1-v3 stay reproducible; they are not edited. Rationale and pricing: docs/implementation/pipeline/ogasp/success_null_overlay_feasibility.md.
value_semantics: overlay_v(src->dst) in [0,1] = given the dispatched verb at src returned verdict v, the conditional likelihood of dst as the next move (0=won't happen, 1=most likely next).
coverage: COMPLETE directed tactic-pair space: 210 = 15*14 (no self-loops). Corpus-AGNOSTIC: every ordered pair is weighted from declared knowledge, so a different CTI/corpus that introduces a new edge is already covered. Which pairs actually ROUTE mass is a base/net property (base=0 => no routing), NOT an overlay property. Self-loop 'retry same tactic' is handled by the stepping layer's bounded-retry, not the overlay.
authoring: CTI-INDEPENDENT declared knowledge only (from v4 on the FAILURE table alone; on success the corpus proportions route unchanged — the base already encodes what successful campaigns did next, and re-weighting it on success would overrule measured proportions with declared values for the same question): lifecycle ordering + capability-enablement + foothold-dependency + lifecycle distance. Values are RULE-GENERATED (first-match-wins, then multiplied by the distance kernel); rationale is stored ONCE per rule, never per pair. The compiler is mtdsim.l3_simulation.controller.rules; `--check` re-compiles every registered version and reports any cell that differs from what is committed.
compiled_views: data/ogasp/controller/overlays/<version>/{success,failure}.json — a registry, one directory per value set that has been run. v1_band_relationship is experiment 1's (bands, no distance); v2_lifecycle_distance is the S1 fold-in; v3_persistent_backward is experiment 2's (delta 0.25); v4_failure_only is the go-forward version from 2026-08-19 (v3's failure table, success as pass-through). See overlays/manifest.json.

relationship.decision: The relationship term (forward / lateral / backward) is read from the four-stage APT-lifecycle consensus, NOT from the five-band kill-chain prior below. Decided 2026-07-28, on the fold-in question lifecycle_consensus.md §5 named. Reason: the distance kernel is defined on the signed consensus stage offset, so reading the relationship from a different ordering would have the same value's two ordering-dependent terms disagree about direction on 40 of 210 pairs — e.g. command-and-control -> discovery is 'backward' under the bands (4 -> 3) while the consensus puts both in stage 2, so the backward tier would fire on a transition the distance term says travels nowhere. One ordering, one direction. It is also the better-grounded ordering: the bands are a declared assumption (M3), while the consensus seats 9 of 15 tactics from model agreement and resolves 5 more by declared rules over sourced inputs.
relationship.cost_stated: The consensus's post-intrusion middle is a single weakly-ordered stage, so 34 of the 40 changed pairs move INTO the lateral class and the middle flattens: success values move 0.6->0.5 (forward->lateral) or 0.25->0.5 (backward->lateral), failure 0.35->0.7 or 0.9->0.7. That is a real loss of discrimination, accepted because the consensus overlay found no lifecycle model that orders consolidation before expansion — the discrimination it removes was asserting an order the literature does not support. The `enables` term still discriminates inside the middle (40 of the 66 within-stage pairs are enabled, hence 1.0), so the middle is not uniform.
relationship.alternative_kept: The five-band prior is retained below, as version v1_band_relationship's ordering and as the provenance of the R2 values experiment 1 ran on.
relationship.not_selected_on_behaviour: The choice was made on coherence and provenance grounds BEFORE any net was walked. The study additionally reports the bands-plus-distance variant as one sensitivity arm, to say whether the choice matters behaviourally — that arm is a report, never the selection criterion.

distance.composition: overlay_v(a->b) = rule_value_v(a->b) * d(a,b) — the distance term MULTIPLIES the first-matching rule's value; it never replaces it and it is not itself a rule.
distance.form: delta = s(b) - s(a) over the consensus stages; d = 1 if delta == 0, gamma^(delta-1) if delta > 0, delta_ratio^(|delta|-1) if delta < 0; then d < z reads as exactly 0 (strict comparison, so a value exactly on the floor survives).
distance.parameters_from: lifecycle_consensus.json declared_parameters — gamma, delta_ratio and z are declared THERE, by the literature half, and read from there rather than restated here.
distance.why_both_verdicts: How far a transition travels across the campaign is a property of the pair, not of the verdict, so the kernel multiplies both treatments. Direction is still encoded, but since Marc's 2026-07-28 ruling it is encoded in the RULE tier rather than in the kernel: on failure a one-step fallback is 0.9 against a forward 0.35, which is where 'back to the drawing board' actually lives.
distance.why_it_also_multiplies_the_gates: A gated pair can be implausible for two independent reasons — the foothold it needs was not won, AND it is a two-stage leap. Both apply, so both multiply.
distance.enablement_cross_check: No pair in enables_on_success has |delta| >= 2 under the consensus stages (histogram: 4 at -1, 40 at 0, 25 at +1). The enables sets were built from MITRE tactic semantics and the AAR get-in/spread sequences, independently of any lifecycle model, so their being adjacency-respecting is an independent corroboration of the consensus ordering rather than a consequence of it — and it is why the distance term leaves the enablement tier untouched at the declared parameters.
distance.kernel_symmetry_note: With gamma = delta_ratio = 0.25 the forward and backward kernels are now NUMERICALLY IDENTICAL, and that is a deliberate consequence of the persistence ruling rather than an oversight. The original design gave them separate parameters so that falling back could be treated as ordinary while leaping forward was suppressed; the ruling is that a FULL-CAMPAIGN fallback is not ordinary either, which removes the reason for the kernels to differ. The near-distance asymmetry the design wanted survives untouched at one stage (both kernels are 1.0 there, and the rule tier makes backward 0.9 against forward 0.35). The two parameters are kept separate rather than collapsed into one so the distinction remains available if the ruling is revisited.

distance_rule.parameters_note: This ledger entry carries `parameters` where every other carries a single `value`: the term is a kernel with three declared constants rather than one number. The schema extension is recorded in declared_value_provenance.md §3.
distance_rule.rationale: a transition's likelihood falls with how many lifecycle stages it crosses, sharply forward and gently backward, so a jump across the whole campaign is not weighted like a step to the adjacent stage
distance_rule.provenance_tier: attested-pattern/declared-magnitude for the decay PATTERN and for gamma (five lifecycle models all chain phase to successor, none draws a recon-to-objective edge); declared-judgement for delta_ratio and z (the backward magnitude now rests on a persistence argument the models do not state, and the floor is a rounding choice).
distance_rule.scrutiny: Grounded in the lifecycle consensus overlay (lifecycle_consensus.md, Marc greenlit 2026-07-27) rather than in this layer's judgement. Swept over its declared bands by the S1 sensitivity study, which is the defence the magnitudes get in place of a citation. Independent corroboration: the enables sets, built with no lifecycle model in hand, contain no pair crossing two or more stages.
changelog: R3 (2026-07-28, S1): NEW term. Folded the declared kernel from lifecycle_consensus.json §6 into the value as a multiplicative factor, and moved the relationship term onto the same consensus ordering. No R2 rule value changed. Effect on the compiled table: 6 pairs per verdict go to exactly 0 (preparation sources -> objective destinations, the canonical long jump), 22 forward pairs are cut to a quarter, 22 backward pairs to a half, 6 deep-backward pairs to a quarter, and the 154 within-stage-or-adjacent pairs are untouched.

2026-07-28 (Marc's ruling): delta_ratio 0.5 -> 0.25. The first value made a full-campaign collapse after a failure 4x less likely than a one-step fallback but not impossible (exfiltration -> reconnaissance sat at 0.0625); the ruling is that an attacker persistent enough to reach exfiltration does not abandon its foothold to re-scan the perimeter, so the three-stage backward jump should fall under the floor and read as exactly 0, as the three-stage forward leap already does. Shipped as overlay version v3_persistent_backward; v2 is frozen for the two studies that consumed it.

passthrough_rule.rationale: the multiplicative identity: on a success verdict the walk is the corpus's own routing. The base flow proportions are taken from reports of campaigns that worked, so base(a->b) already answers 'given success at a, where next'; a declared success matrix re-encodes that answer at a weaker tier and overrules the measured proportions wherever it differs. Nothing declared multiplies a success verdict from v4 on — not the rules and not the distance kernel.
passthrough_rule.provenance_tier: corpus-grounded (by deference: the value declares nothing; the corpus proportions carry the success routing)
passthrough_rule.scrutiny: Marc's 2026-08-19 ruling on the feasibility study (success_null_overlay_feasibility.md): statically the retired success table moved 13-20% of out-mass at a conditioned place; behaviourally its removal is a profile-signed 1-3 host effect through the enables tier's coupling to the mapping (objective_none_c2 up, objective_exfiltration_impact down), no experiment-2 headline moved. The evidence-tier inversion (the success table was the better-attested half) is weighed there: what it dropped was a re-declaration of the same survivorship evidence the base is built from, not the evidence.
